correctness.rationale: Inductively upper-bound the optimal continuation V_(k-1)(Y) by c(Y+(L-1)z), where c is the global supremum ratio, then apply E[Y]=z. Explicit derivative has the unique maximizer u*=z(M/z)^(1/k) for L>1, and the two-point law exactly attains the affine bound. The base k=1 and L=1 are treated separately. Convexity establishes monotonicity and Taylor expansion gives the sharp first-order gap. A standalone executable passed symbolic identities, rational instances and 15,375 finite inequalities; the analytic proof is the universal certificate.

originality.rationale: The original 2026 paper explicitly supplies the equal-multiplier attainable probability but only an unbounded-time upper bound. The new finite-N universal upper bound over all history-dependent fair lotteries, strict optimal-law characterization, and sharp rate are not implied. Classical 2007–08 finite-horizon bold play fixes casino odds and disallows negative stakes/fortunes, so does not cover the present admissible controls. Four actual published-finding corpus queries and own-ledger claim checks yielded no covering item, subject to residual general-theorem and inaccessible-source risks.
residual_risks: An unlocated general finite-horizon concave-envelope or martingale-control theorem might imply the sharp value and uniqueness.

Search coverage, including published-finding corpus and accessible historical records, cannot mathematically certify universal originality.
